summary: Settlements and volume accountants find that a counterparty invoice, statement or payment disagrees with the deal booked in Sitara. Today they email the trader one deal at a time and wait, often right up to an invoice or payment deadline. A pre-invoice match job compares each counterparty line with the Sitara deal price and volume, sends the trader a queue of cases that already hold both figures, and writes the confirmed answer back so Unify can redraft. That removes most of the research and chasing, worth about $110 per month ($1,320 per year).

current_workflow.step: A counterparty statement, invoice or payment arrives, and a settlements or volume accountant compares it by hand with the deal ticket in Sitara, deal by deal.
current_workflow.who: settlements / volume accounting (e.g. Megan Parker, Katherine Herrera, Lauri Allen)

current_workflow.step: When a price, rate or volume differs, or the counterparty does not recognise the deal at all, the accountant writes a free-text email to the trader or logistics desk. The email holds the deal number, both figures and a question about which one is correct.
current_workflow.who: settlements accountant to trader / logistics desk (Daren Farmer)

current_workflow.step: The trader looks back at the deal, sometimes having to ask the counterparty's trader or a third party for the deal terms, and confirms the price or agrees to dispute it.
If the trader is unavailable, the accountant escalates or asks someone else to change the deal so the invoice can still go out on time.
The desk corrects the Sitara deal, settlements redraft the invoice in Unify, and a corrected invoice goes to the counterparty. Commercial conditions may first have to be discussed before billing.

stall_points.description: The mismatch is found only after the counterparty's figures arrive. The accountant then has to ask the trader which price is right, under time pressure.
stall_points.quote: We have HSC -0.05 and Mitchell shows HSC - 0.04.

stall_points.description: The counterparty does not have the deal booked at all, so payment stops until the trader goes back to the other side's trader. Invoices are due the same day.

stall_points.description: Sitara was not updated with the month's price, so the Unify invoice had to be redrafted after the fact.

solution.approach: Counterparty statements, invoices and payment remittances are loaded into a staging table as they arrive, one row per deal, day and point. A match job joins each row to the Sitara deal ticket by deal number, or by counterparty, point and production month when no number is given. It compares price or index formula, volume and transport rate, and flags differences above a tolerance, missing deals and zero-rate tickets. Each flagged row becomes a case in a shared discrepancy queue. A case holds the deal number, both figures, the invoice due date and the trader from the Sitara ticket, and is routed to that trader with a backup named for each desk. The trader picks 'Sitara correct', 'counterparty correct' or 'dispute'. Choosing 'counterparty correct' produces a prefilled Sitara change request, and after the change is made settlements are told to redraft in Unify. The same match also runs on the desk's own booked deals before invoices go out, so stale prices like the August Agave case are caught before the invoice rather than after it.
solution.trigger: Arrival of a counterparty statement, invoice or payment in settlements, plus a scheduled pre-invoice run in the days before invoices are sent each production month
inputs: counterparty statements, invoices and payment remittances (deal number, production month, day, point, volume, price or rate)
Sitara deal tickets (deal number, counterparty, trader, price or index formula, volume, term, transport rate)
invoice drafts and due dates from Unify
desk booking positions in Tagg where a deal is valued there
outputs: discrepancy cases for the responsible trader, holding both figures, the deal number and the due date
prefilled Sitara deal change requests when the counterparty figure is confirmed
a redraft notice to settlements when the Sitara change is made
a dispute record that settlements send to the counterparty when the Sitara figure is confirmed
a daily aging list of open cases sorted by invoice due date, for the settlements lead
components: counterparty statement intake and staging table (manual upload at first, with a parser for recurring statement layouts)
deal match and tolerance comparison job
discrepancy case queue with trader routing and backup escalation
decision form (Sitara correct / counterparty correct / dispute) that produces a prefilled deal change request
pre-invoice stale-price check and aging report

implementation_steps: Pull a sample of recent counterparty statements from settlements (Midcon, Mitchell Gas Services, DEFS, Hesco, Southern Union, Texas General Land Office) and list the fields each one carries.
Build the staging table and a manual upload template, with deal number, production month, day, point, volume and price, so accountants can load any statement on day one.
Write the match job against a read-only Sitara extract. Join by deal number first, then by counterparty, point and month, and agree price and volume tolerances with settlements.
Set up the case queue. Route each case by the trader on the Sitara ticket and assign a named backup per desk for when the trader is out.
Add the decision form. Have 'counterparty correct' produce a Sitara change request for deal entry, and send settlements a Unify redraft notice once Sitara is updated.
Add the scheduled pre-invoice run that flags zero-rate tickets and months with no price entered before invoices are drafted.
Run alongside the current email process for one production month, compare the cases with the emails actually sent, then switch settlements over to the queue.
Add parsers for the highest-volume counterparty statement layouts after the pilot.
stays_manual: Deciding which price is correct: only the trader knows what was agreed, as the Mitchell and DEFS cases show.
Approving and keying any change to a Sitara deal ticket, which stays under existing deal-entry controls.
Contacting the counterparty's trader when they have no record of the deal or dispute what it covers (Midcon, Texas General Land Office).
Commercial judgments such as holding billing until side conditions are discussed (the Transwestern capacity release case).
Penalty or imbalance charges that the counterparty raises and that are not tied to a single deal line.
risks: Counterparty statements come in many layouts and some carry no deal number. Mitigate with a manual upload template first, and add parsers only for the high-volume layouts.

Index-based prices (for example HSC minus a differential) need formula comparison rather than a single number. Compare the formula and the differential, and flag any case where the index cannot be resolved for a human to look at.
Tolerances that are too tight flood traders with noise. Tune them during the parallel month and track how often traders mark cases 'Sitara correct'.
The evidence does not show how Unify or Tagg export data or what access is available. Confirm extract access with IT before committing to the M estimate.
Traders may keep answering by email. The settlements lead should send email requests back to the queue, and the aging report makes overdue cases visible.
The value estimate rests on a sampled median handling time. Measure actual time per case during the pilot.
success_metric: Median hours from discrepancy detected to trader decision, and the share of invoices redrafted in Unify after being sent, measured per production month before and after rollout
